The coherence pass merged first as open-platform-model/core#41, so the release commit sits on top of it and the published tag includes it — the ordering the change's own schema-release capability requires, since a stale cross-reference is defined to block the cut. THE SINGLE CUT POINT NEVER HAPPENED, and this event closes the question the 2026-08-07 event above left open by recording which way it went: the slice is closed as done-differently rather than rescoped. The four slices shipped across four alphas — alpha.1 core-identity-shape plus the major move, alpha.2 core-primitive-keying, alpha.3 core-platform-and-match, alpha.4 core-identity-package — so what this slice actually delivered was the coherence pass and the verification, not the cut. THE PROPOSAL'S PARTIAL-TAG WARNING IS NARROWER THAN THE FACTS and is corrected here, because the next slice retargets against it: it names v2.0.0-alpha.1 as the dangerous resolvable-but-incomplete tag. alpha.2 and alpha.3 are partial too, and alpha.3 is the MOST hazardous of the three — it carries three of the four slices, so it compiles far enough to look complete and fails only on the identity package. Only alpha.4 is a retarget target. THE COHERENCE PASS FOUND SEVEN DEFECTS, all editorial, none design, so nothing blocked. The one that changes a claim other documents rest on: SPEC.md 3.6 and 5.2, identity_package.cue's doc comment and identity_package_pins.cue's note all said the scalar-subscription reshape REMOVED the platform-side major-agreement backstop that D43 and D45 accepted their exposure against. It removed nothing. Verified independently rather than copied from 0011's own correction — `git log --all -S_majorAgrees -- src/` is empty at every commit, and the pre-reshape subscription filter carried only range/allow/deny. The check was never built in `core`. The exposure is unchanged; the OWNERSHIP is not, and that is the part worth carrying: an unbuilt check belongs to library-subscription-collapse, which is `status: planned` and has a landing point, where a deleted one would be a regression this repo introduced and nobody holds. All four sites now say so. ALSO FOUND: two sections disagreed on grouping segments, 3.3 admitting what 5.2, 5.3 and #CatalogMemberFQNGate refuse, with D42 settling it — corrected in SPEC.md, in two doc comments, and in the identity_pins.cue and platform_and_match_pins.cue fixtures, which had modelled a path the sibling gate file's own MUST-FAIL case rejects; a version number wrong in three places (the filter went in alpha.3, not alpha.4); #Secret listed as a Primitive despite carrying no metadata, apiVersion, contract key or spec; #Blueprint's section sitting under the Constructs heading while two other places call it a primitive; D32's `fulfilment cannot be derived` resting on a premise D42 invalidated, with the conclusion re-grounded on a member's path carrying no major and D32 itself untouched; and docs/ still describing the pre-0010 schema throughout, including #Component.metadata.labels documented as unified from its primitives — the exact claim D36 deleted, contradicting corrected prose 26 lines below it in the same file. D41 VERIFIED AGAINST THE PUBLISHED ARTIFACT, not against the source tree: a scratch module resolving from ghcr.io anonymously confirms module uuid is unchanged when only version moves and moves when the path's major moves, while instance uuid survives BOTH — both halves of the invariant, from a tree that did not build it. #IdentityPackage and #CatalogMemberFQNGate are reachable by a consumer and kindPrefix returns one segment per kind. ROLLBACK BOUNDARY, recorded here because the next slice is where it closes: re-pinning to opmodel.dev/core@v1 at v1.1.0-alpha.1 stays available to every consumer until library-core-retarget merges. It is an IMPORT REWRITE now, not a version pin — every `import opmodel.dev/core@v1` becomes the v2 line alongside the cue.mod edit, and `task update-deps` cannot do it, because resolving a new major is not the same operation as raising a version within one. Both majors stay resolvable indefinitely, since a published tag names fixed bytes permanently, so the old line does not rot; it only gets more expensive to return to. | [0013](./0013/) | cross-cutting | draft | - | not-started | 2026-07-27 — Design revised on review: D10 supersedes D1, D11 supersedes D4, D12 amends D9, and OQ1 is closed. D1 had removed the `#Secret` contract type AND the disjunction inside it, when only the routing metadata needed to move to the attribute — leaving the deployer no slot in which to say "this Secret already exists", and forcing the handle-plus-context-map machinery of D4 to compensate. D10 restores `#Secret` narrowed to `#SecretLiteral | #SecretRef`, so the ATTRIBUTE carries routing (author intent, static, in the published module) and the TYPE carries fulfilment (deployer choice, per environment, type-checked by CUE). D11 replaces handle substitution with resolve-in-place: the kernel rewrites every secret to its `#SecretRef` form, so both arms converge before render, a transformer reads two fields from one branch, and the whole handle format, the `#TransformerContext` addition, the `owned` flag and the output scanner are all deleted. Three properties fall out that the first draft lacked: instance files for supplied secrets do not change at all, plaintext in the render is structurally unrepresentable rather than stripped, and a secret interpolated into a rendered string fails at plain `cue vet` at authoring time. Experiment 02 rebuilt as `02-resolve-in-place` and re-run: all five claims held, and its Go content hash agrees with the CUE one in examples.cue. OQ2 opened — whether the arm rewrite survives the real kernel build path — and is now the sole blocker to acceptance. | Attribute-Declared Secret Fields |

| [0015](./0015/) | cross-cutting | draft | - | not-started | 2026-08-05 — Drafted from a design conversation grounded in three measurements taken the same day. `core/src/catalog.cue` carries exactly ONE member map, `#transformers`, and `library/opm/materialize/index.go:39-41` skips any catalog build without one — so a contract with no adapter is absent from the materialized world, which is precisely the state 0010 D37's `fulfilment: "provider"` creates on purpose. `compile/match.go:344-360` is SUBSET containment, not equality, so a more-specific transformer never displaces a less-specific one; both pair and both render, and 0010 D32's guard does not reach the case because it fires only for `fulfilment: "provider"` contracts. And the real discriminator across the 8 transformers sharing `catalog_opm`'s `#ContainerResource` bucket is `requiredLabels` (`daemonset_transformer.cue:27-29`), not the resource/trait set — which is what makes 0010 D36's `matchLabels` the lever for provider classes rather than a new matcher concept. Four decisions locked: D1 (explicit contract maps), D2 (classes, amending 0010 D37), D3 (RBAC-gated registration CR), D4 (no contract/adapter packaging split, decided now because riding 0010's FQN break is nearly free and a standalone break later is not). Six Open Questions carried. | Catalog Contracts, Provider Classes, and Transformer Registration |

## Status legend

- **draft** — initial design, actively being written
- **accepted** — design agreed upon, ready for implementation
- **implemented** — design has been realized in code
- **superseded** — replaced by a newer enhancement (see `superseded_by` in the entry's config.yaml)
